headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir sworn in as 23rd president of Bangladesh
summary: The BNP-nominated candidate took the oath of office at Bangabhaban on Friday evening, following a victory in the National Parliament election.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially taken the oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The swearing-in ceremony took place at Bangabhaban on Friday evening, shortly after 7:30 PM.
The oath was administered by Barrister Kaiser Kamal, the Acting Speaker of the National Parliament. The event was managed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani and began with a prayer session.
The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, the Chief Justice, cabinet members, foreign diplomats, members of parliament, and high-ranking civil and military officials.
Mr. Fakhrul was elected on Thursday in a National Parliament vote, securing 255 votes. His sole opponent, opposition-nominated candidate Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, received 88 votes.
A total of 343 out of 349 eligible voters cast their ballots in the presidential election. Chief Election Commissioner A M M Nasir Uddin officially declared Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir the winner.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd President of Bangladesh after winning 255 votes in the National Parliament.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has officially taken the oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The swearing-in ceremony took place at Bangabhaban on Friday evening, shortly after 7:30 PM.

The oath was administered by Barrister Kaiser Kamal, the Acting Speaker of the National Parliament. The event was managed by Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Gani and began with a prayer session.

The ceremony was attended by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, the Chief Justice, cabinet members, foreign diplomats, members of parliament, and high-ranking civil and military officials.

Mr. Fakhrul was elected on Thursday in a National Parliament vote, securing 255 votes. His sole opponent, opposition-nominated candidate Colonel (Retd) Oli Ahmed, received 88 votes.

A total of 343 out of 349 eligible voters cast their ballots in the presidential election. Chief Election Commissioner A M M Nasir Uddin officially declared Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir the winner.

headline: Six new members join BNP-led cabinet on Friday
summary: Four ministers and two state ministers took their oaths at Bangabhaban, following the swearing-in of the 23rd President of Bangladesh.
details: Six new members joined the cabinet of the BNP-led government under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. The ceremony took place at the Bangabhaban Darbar Hall on Friday evening.
The new ministers include Dr. Abdul Moyeen Khan (Narsingdi-2), Barrister Andaleeve Rahman Partho (Bhola-1), Saching Pru Jerry (Bandarban), and M Rashiduzzaman Millat (Jamalpur-1).
M Rashiduzzaman Millat, who previously served as the State Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism, has now been promoted to a full cabinet minister.
Additionally, Humayun Rashid, the Prime Minister's foreign affairs advisor, and Mohammad Shamim Kaiser Lincoln (Gaibandha-4) were sworn in as state ministers.
The oaths were administered by the newly sworn-in 23rd President of Bangladesh, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, who took his own oath of office shortly before the ceremony.
caption:
Six new faces enter the cabinet. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir takes oath as the 23rd President of Bangladesh.

Six new members joined the cabinet of the BNP-led government under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. The ceremony took place at the Bangabhaban Darbar Hall on Friday evening.

The new ministers include Dr. Abdul Moyeen Khan (Narsingdi-2), Barrister Andaleeve Rahman Partho (Bhola-1), Saching Pru Jerry (Bandarban), and M Rashiduzzaman Millat (Jamalpur-1).

M Rashiduzzaman Millat, who previously served as the State Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism, has now been promoted to a full cabinet minister.

Additionally, Humayun Rashid, the Prime Minister's foreign affairs advisor, and Mohammad Shamim Kaiser Lincoln (Gaibandha-4) were sworn in as state ministers.

The oaths were administered by the newly sworn-in 23rd President of Bangladesh, Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, who took his own oath of office shortly before the ceremony.
